english.title: Subject of a Football Banning Order fail to comply with a section 19(2) requirement
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the subject of a football banning order made under section 15 of the Football Spectators Act 1989, failed, without reasonable excuse, to comply with a requirement imposed upon you on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE..) under section 19(2) of the said Act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(6) and (7) of the Football Spectators Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) The Football (Offences and Disorder) Act 1999 provided that 'International Football Banning Order' should replace the term 'Restriction Order' in the Football Spectators Act 1989 from 27.9.99. Officers should take care when using this heading that the order being breached was in fact issued on or after that date and before 28.8.2000 when the Football (Disorder) Act 2000 merged International and Domestic Football Banning Orders into Banning Orders.
(ii) Where an Order was issued prior to 27.9.99 the offence wording in relation to 'Restriction Orders' should be used - see H3441.
(iii) See offence wordings H3440 and H4268 for failing to comply with a Restriction Order / International Football Banning Order, as appropriate.
(iv) Although the issuing of International Football Banning Orders has now lapsed, it is feasible that the date for expiry of such an order could be 28/08/2010 and therefore this offence wording will be valid until that date.
(v) Now PNC recordable from 18/08/07 as per S.I. 2007/2121
